content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from various studies and articles, primarily related to pharmaceutical pricing, health technology assessments, and drug policy reforms across different countries. Each entry includes the title of the study, the authors, the journal, the year of publication, and a note indicating Insufficient Data. 1. The study titled Immune Indications: An EU5 Perspective was published in Value in Health in 2018 (Volume 21, Page S260). It discusses immune-related indications within the context of the EU5 countries. However, the data provided is insufficient for conclusive analysis. 2. Eheberg D, Batscheider A, Lebioda A, Plantör S, and Fricke FU examined the impact of Germany's Pharmaceutical Market Reorganization Act (AMNOG) on the reference price market two years after its implementation. Their findings, published in Value in Health in 2012 (Volume 15, Issue 7, Page A324), highlight trends but lack sufficient data for definitive conclusions. 3. Eheberg D, Pointner J, Antoni B, Gossmann JA, and Batscheider A explored the role of biosimilars and reference price groups in Germany. Their work, published in Value in Health in 2016 (Volume 19, Issue 7, Page A468), provides insights but is limited by insufficient data. 4. Fedyayev D, Fedyaeva VK, and Omelyanovskiy VV analyzed government procurement of medicines for rare diseases in Russia. Their study, published in Value in Health in 2015 (Volume 18, Issue 7, Page A677), lacks sufficient data for comprehensive conclusions. 5. Fernandes MDO, Wehner MVR, Garcia GC, Caldeira TR, Ronchini MAK, and Troncoso GC critically appraised the financial impact of implementing Brazilian pharmaceutical pricing regulations (CMED Resolution No. 2/2004) on new drug prices. Published in Value in Health in 2013 (Volume 16, Issue 3, Page A253), the study is limited by insufficient data. 6. Fontrier A, Efthymiadou A, Boekstein N, Kanavos P, and Gill J investigated the evolution of external price referencing across various countries. Their findings, published in Value in Health in 2016 (Volume 19, Issue 7, Page A497), are constrained by insufficient data. 7. Fukushima A, Dorey J, Kiyabu G, François C, and Toumi M analyzed Japan's 2018 drug pricing system reform aimed at enhancing price containment. Published in Value in Health in 2018 (Volume 21, Page S46), the study provides limited data. 8. García Muñoz C, Alarcón Payer C, Cañamares Orbis I, Jiménez Cerezo MJ, Calleja Hernández MA, and Ferrari Piquer JM evaluated the clinical and financial effects of therapeutic equivalence programs in a tertiary hospital. Their study, published in Aten Farm in 2014 (Volume 16, Issue 4, Pages 250-257), is limited by insufficient data. 9. Ghosh W, Bose R, Viswambaram A, and Brooks-Rooney C examined value-based pricing in Singapore, questioning whether it leads to a race to the bottom. Published in Value in Health in 2018 (Volume 21, Page S9), the study lacks sufficient data. 10. Gibson TB, Mahoney J, Lucas K, Heithoff K, and Gatwood J explored value-based design and prescribing patterns. Their findings, published in Value in Health in 2012 (Volume 15, Issue 4, Page A13), are constrained by insufficient data. 11. Glatz P, Ilavska A, Hloska A, and Filko M analyzed the impact of drug pricing and reimbursement reforms in Slovakia. Published in Value in Health in 2010 (Volume 13, Issue 3, Page A95), the study provides limited data. 12. Godman B, Bennie M, Bucsi A, Hesse U, Martin A, Miranda J, et al. reviewed the availability of generic losartan across Europe and its implications for future policies. Their study, published in Clinical Therapeutics in 2013 (Volume 35, Issue 8, Pages e36-e37), is limited by insufficient data. 13. Godman B, Kurdí A, MacBride-Stewart S, Hurding S, McCabe H, and Morton A assessed initiatives in Scotland to improve prescribing quality and efficiency. Published in Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety in 2018 (Volume 27, Page 430), the study lacks sufficient data. 14. Godman B, Wettermark B, Cankat Tulunay F, Zara C, and Gustafsson LL examined the intensity of reforms and their impact on generic drug utilization across Europe. Published in Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety in 2011 (Volume 20, Issue 6, Pages 662-663), the study provides limited data. 15. Goetz C, Rotman SR, Epstein HAB, and Bishop TF conducted a systematic review on the impact of price transparency on medical decisions and practices. Published in Journal of General Internal Medicine in 2013 (Volume 28, Page S218), the study is constrained by insufficient data. 16. Goodman C, Villarivera C, Gregor KJ, and van Bavel J analyzed opportunities for reform in the pharmaceutical market. Published in Value in Health in 2018 (Volume 21, Page S209), the study lacks sufficient data. 17. Guan Y reviewed the evolution of international reference pricing in China. Published in Value in Health in 2016 (Volume 19, Issue 7, Page A835), the study provides limited data. 18. Hammerman A, Feder-Bubis P, and Greenberg D evaluated financial risk-sharing schemes for new technologies in Israel's national health services. Published in Value in Health in 2010 (Volume 13, Issue 7, Page A428), the study is constrained by insufficient data. 19. Hao Y analyzed health technology assessment and value-based pricing developments in Germany, the UK, and France. Published in Value in Health in 2013 (Volume 16, Issue 3, Page A261), the study lacks sufficient data. 20. Hartmann M, Droeschel D, Vollmer L, De Paz B, and Walzer S assessed access to innovative cancer drugs and the divergent outcomes of HTA appraisals in France, Germany, and the UK. Published in European Journal of Cancer in 2017 (Volume 72, Page S115), the study provides limited data.
